annotationRationale: Recognizing the difference-of-squares product is the decisive step. Squaring each square root recovers its radicand.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official method: multiply the known difference by the desired sum so that the terms involving x cancel.

review.mathCheck: The difference times the requested sum is \(49-x^2-(25-x^2)=24\), so \(3S=24\) and \(S=8\), choice A. The premise is consistent: the radicals can be \(11/2\) and \(5/2\), with \(x^2=75/4\).
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the first MAA solution 10 (p. 3). Defining only the requested sum preserves the official conjugate-product method. Solving for x is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Difference of squares is correctly assessed and square-root properties are supporting knowledge. The given real equation already ensures defined radicals; this method introduces no extraneous candidates.
